lead: Movable appliances that heat, cool, move, clean or dry the air of a room — heaters, window and portable air conditioners, fans, air purifiers, humidifiers and dehumidifiers — organised by what the appliance does to the air, then by kind, with built-in heating, cooling, ventilation, water and energy systems living in Home Fixtures & Features.

depts.note: Plug-in or fuel-fed heaters a person moves between rooms; stoves, fires, boilers, radiators and towel rails are built-ins and move to G3.

b.m: Heat output matched to the room
b.v: kW or BTU; W per m² rule of thumb
b.w: Size comes before anything else; Which? and Consumer Reports both test by room size.

b.v: pence or cents per hour at rated power; fuel type
b.w: Electric heaters are all near 100% efficient, so cost is set by tariff and fuel, not by the heater.

b.v: tip-over and overheat cut-outs; CO and oxygen-depletion sensors on gas and kerosene
b.w: Portable heaters lead home-fire statistics; unflued fuel heaters add CO risk.
Fan heaters run close to people; oil and panel heaters are silent.
Features come after output and safety.

depts.t: Plug-in or fuel-fed heaters moved from room to room; a fixed stove, boiler or radiator → Home Fixtures (G3); a patio heater → C2.
depts.ax: How does the heater make and deliver warmth: by warming the air, by a radiant beam, or by a flame or fuel?

s.t: Electric heaters that warm the air around them: fan heaters, convectors and oil-filled radiators; a beam of radiant heat → Radiant heaters.
s.ax: kinds by how the warm air moves: blown by a fan, rising by convection, held in oil

k.a: blow heater · ceramic heater · PTC heater · hot and cool fan
k.d: Room heater that blows air over a heating element, usually a ceramic PTC element, for fast local warmth.

k.a: convection heater · panel heater · micathermic heater
k.d: Room heater that warms air rising over an element by natural convection, without a fan or oil.

k.a: oil heater · column heater · oil-filled heater
k.d: Portable electric heater whose element warms sealed oil inside finned columns, giving slow, steady, quiet heat.

s.t: Electric heaters that beam infrared heat at people and objects: bar and halogen heaters, heat lamps and wall panels; a heater that blows warm air → Warm-air heaters.

k.a: bar heater · halogen heater · quartz heater · carbon heater · heat lamp
k.d: Heater whose glowing element and reflector beam infrared heat directly at people and objects in front of it.

k.a: far-infrared panel · IR heating panel · picture heater · mirror heater
k.d: Flat, low-temperature plug-in panel hung on a wall or ceiling that heats people and surfaces by far-infrared radiation.

s.t: Heaters with a real or imitated flame, or that burn fuel: electric fire stoves, kerosene and bottled-gas heaters; a fixed fire or stove → G3.
s.ax: kinds by what makes the flame: electricity, kerosene, bottled gas

k.a: electric fire · electric stove · flame-effect heater
k.d: Freestanding plug-in electric stove or fire with a flame effect that can run with or without heat; inset and wall-mounted units are in Home Fixtures.

k.a: paraffin heater · kerosene stove · oil fan heater
k.d: Portable unvented heater that burns kerosene from a built-in tank, by wick or by electrically assisted vaporising burner.

k.a: cabinet heater · bottled-gas heater · catalytic heater · propane heater
k.d: Flueless room heater burning bottled butane or propane, as a wheeled cabinet or compact radiant or catalytic unit; needs ventilation and an oxygen depletion sensor.

depts.note: Window and portable air conditioners and evaporative coolers; split, cassette and ducted systems are fixtures (G3).

b.m: Cooling capacity matched to the room
b.v: BTU/h or kW; SACC for portables (US DOE)
b.w: Portable units are rated by SACC, which is lower than the headline BTU.

b.v: CEER (US window units); EU energy label

b.w: Bedroom use decides most purchases; RTINGS and Consumer Reports publish dB.
Dual-hose portables cool better; drainage sets convenience.

depts.t: Movable or window-fitted appliances that cool room air; a fixed split or ducted system → Home Fixtures (G3); a fan that only moves air → Fans.
depts.ax: How does it cool the air: with a refrigerant circuit or by evaporating water?

s.t: Refrigerant units that cool and dry room air: window, through-the-wall and portable hose models; a fixed split system → G3.
s.ax: kinds by where the unit sits: in a window or wall, or on the floor with a hose

k.a: window unit · room air conditioner · through-the-wall AC · U-shaped AC · saddle AC
k.d: Single-box refrigerant unit fitted in a window or wall sleeve, with the condenser outdoors and the cold side indoors.
tt: U-shaped / saddle (sash closes through the gap)

k.a: PAC · mobile air conditioner · floor-standing AC · monobloc
k.d: Movable single-box refrigerant unit on castors that exhausts heat outdoors through a window hose.

s.t: Units that cool air by evaporating water, adding humidity: room, desert and outdoor coolers and misting fans; a refrigerant unit → Air conditioners.

k.a: swamp cooler · desert cooler · air cooler · wet air cooler
k.d: Fan that blows air through a water-soaked pad to cool by evaporation; adds humidity, so suits dry climates and is not an air conditioner.

k.a: mist fan · water-spray fan · patio misting fan
k.d: Fan that sprays a fine water mist into its airflow to cool by evaporation, for patios and hot dry rooms; a plain fan → Fans.

depts.note: Plug-in and battery fans that move air to cool a person or mix a room; ceiling fans and extractor fans are fixtures (G3).

b.v: CFM or m³/min; oscillation; DC motor
b.w: Fans are compared on airflow per watt and noise, not on power.
Bedroom use decides most purchases; RTINGS and Consumer Reports publish dB.

depts.t: Fans that move air without heating, cooling or cleaning it; a fan that also heats → Portable heating; a fixed ceiling or extractor fan → G3.
depts.ax: Where does the fan stand, mount or travel: on a table or floor, on a window or wall, or on the body?

s.t: Fans with their own base that cool a person or circulate room air: desk, box, floor, pedestal and tower fans and air circulators.
s.ax: kinds by where the base sits: table, floor, stand, column, then the circulator that moves room air

k.a: Table fan · tabletop fan · personal fan
k.d: Small fan made to stand on a desk or table and cool one person.
m: Turbo Silence Extreme Desk Fan VU2730

k.a: Square fan
k.d: Portable fan with its blade set in a square box frame, standing on the floor or in a window.
m: Classic Series 20 in. Floor Box Fan

k.a: low-profile fan · drum fan · high-velocity fan
k.d: Fan that sits on the floor with no stand and blows across the room, larger than a desk fan; on a stand → Pedestal fan.

k.a: Stand fan · standing fan · stationary fan · floor fan
k.d: Fan on a stand or pedestal of adjustable height, usually oscillating, for a whole room.
m: Turbo Silence Extreme Stand Fan VU5670

k.a: Column fan
k.d: Tall, narrow fan blowing through a vertical grille, usually oscillating with remote and timer.
m: QuietSet Whole Room Tower Fan HYF290

k.a: Whole-room circulator · vortex fan
k.d: Fan made to move air round a whole room in a focused stream rather than cool one person.

s.t: Fans fixed to a window opening, wall or clip rather than standing: window fans, wall fans and clip fans.

k.d: Fan made to fit in a window opening to draw air in or blow it out, single or twin, often reversible.
m: BW2300 Twin Reversible Airflow Window Fan

k.a: Wall-mount fan · clip-on fan · stroller fan
k.d: Fan made to mount on a wall or clip to an edge, cot or pram.

s.t: Powered fans held or worn so they cool one person on the move: handheld and neck fans.

k.a: hand fan (powered) · mini fan
k.d: Powered fan held in the hand; a plain folding hand fan is a fashion accessory.

k.a: wearable fan · neck air conditioner · waist fan
k.d: Powered fan worn on the neck, waist or a clip so it cools hands-free; a hand-held fan → Handheld fan.

s.t: Electric fans collected or chosen for their maker and design, from early brass-blade table fans to bladeless designer fans.

k.a: collectable fan · antique fan · designer fan
k.d: Electric fans collected or chosen for their maker and design, from early brass-blade table fans to bladeless and DC-motor designer fans.

v.d: Example held by the National Museum of American History

x.dt: table · floor · stand · window · size small to large

x.d: Bladeless fan that draws air through a base and projects it from a ring-shaped aperture.

Heater that also runs as a fan; early units recalled for fire risk

depts.note: Room appliances that filter or treat air, their filters, and monitors that measure it; whole-house and ducted units are fixtures (G3).

b.m: Clean-air delivery rate for the room
b.v: CADR (AHAM) smoke/dust/pollen; m²; 4.8 air changes per hour
b.w: CADR is the independent yardstick used by AHAM, Which?, Consumer Reports and Wirecutter.

b.v: HEPA H13/true HEPA; activated carbon; filter price per year
b.w: Filters cost more than the machine over its life.

b.v: dB on sleep and top settings

depts.t: Appliances that clean room air, the filters made for them, and small monitors that measure it; a CO or smoke alarm → B8; a humidifier → Humidity control.
depts.ax: Does it clean the air, supply the filters that clean it, or only measure it?

s.t: Movable air cleaners and the filters made to fit them: HEPA purifiers and replacement cartridges.

k.a: air cleaner · HEPA purifier · purifying fan · air deodoriser · ion generator · ioniser
k.d: Movable appliance that filters or treats room air to remove particles, odours and gases; sold by room size, CADR and filter grade.
r: Blue Pure, Blue Signature, HealthProtect and Classic Pro

k.a: purifier filter · HEPA filter cartridge · carbon filter · humidifier wick · dehumidifier filter
k.d: Consumable filter or wick made to fit a specific air purifier, humidifier or dehumidifier; genuine maker filters or cheaper third-party equivalents.
m: Core 300 replacement filter (Original, Pet Allergy, Smoke Remover, Toxin Absorber)

s.t: Small room devices that measure carbon dioxide, particles, VOCs or radon; a CO alarm → B8.

k.a: IAQ monitor · CO2 monitor · PM2.5 monitor · air quality sensor
k.d: Small room device that measures carbon dioxide, fine particles, VOCs, humidity or radon and shows readings on a display or app; CO alarms sit in B8, weather stations in E6.

depts.note: Room humidifiers, dehumidifiers and moisture absorbers; whole-house units are fixtures (G3).

b.v: litres or pints per day at the rated condition (DOE 65°F/60% RH; 30°C/80% RH)
b.w: Shoppers choose humidifiers and dehumidifiers by capacity first.

b.v: dB on sleep and top settings

b.w: Humidifier hygiene depends on cleaning; Wirecutter weights it heavily.

depts.t: Appliances that add moisture to room air or take it out; a scent diffuser → B4; a whole-house unit → Home Fixtures (G3).
depts.ax: Does it add moisture to the air or take it out?

s.t: Appliances that put water into the air as mist or steam: ultrasonic, evaporative and warm-mist humidifiers; a scent diffuser → B4.

k.a: room humidifier · cool-mist humidifier · vaporiser · air washer
k.d: Appliance that adds moisture to room air by ultrasonic mist, evaporative wick or disc, or warm mist and steam.

s.t: Powered or unpowered appliances that draw water out of the air: compressor and desiccant dehumidifiers and calcium-chloride absorbers.
s.ax: kinds by whether it needs power: powered dehumidifier, then unpowered absorber

k.a: room dehumidifier · portable dehumidifier · mini dehumidifier · desiccant dehumidifier
k.d: Powered appliance that pulls water from room air with a refrigerant coil or desiccant rotor, rated in litres or pints per day.

k.a: moisture trap · damp trap · hanging moisture absorber
k.d: Unpowered tub or hanging bag of calcium-chloride crystals that absorbs moisture from a cupboard, caravan or small room.
m: Aero 360 Moisture Absorber with Refill Tab
Damp Clear Moisture Absorber Refill Granules

ax: What does the appliance do to the air of a room: warm it, cool it, move it, clean it or change its moisture?
key: 1. Does it make the room warmer, by plug-in element or by burning fuel? → Portable heating
2. Does it cool the air with a refrigerant circuit or by evaporating water? → Air conditioners & coolers
3. Does it only move air, to cool a person or mix the room, standing, mounted or worn? → Fans
4. Does it filter or treat the air, or measure its quality? → Air cleaning & monitoring
5. Does it add moisture to the air or draw it out? → Humidity control

Precedence: a fan that heats is a heater (step 1); a fan with a water spray is an evaporative cooler (step 2); a purifier built into a fan is a purifier (step 4); fixed ceiling, extractor and split systems belong to Home Fixtures (G3).
